full_judgment: 25. The petitioner has argued before us that he was all along in service and his inability to render service to his employer between the dates 11-3-1991 to 18-11-2007 was not due to his fault and it was the authority which kept him away from the service. He had placed before the employer the decision of the Appellate Division in the case of The Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary. Ministry of Establishment vs Shamsuddin Ahmed, 1 ADC (2004) 144, where it was held by the Appellate Division that the learned Advocate on behalf of the appellant-government had submitted that the absence of five years from duty continuously would be hit by Rule, 195 of the SR (Service Rule) Part 1. But the Appellate Division held that the respondent was not absent from duty. He was prevented from joining his duties because of the order of removal and Rule 195 has no application. The petitioner before us has argued that since he was all along able and willing to join his post and it was the respondents who restrained him from joining, the absence cannot be said to be due to his fault and, therefore, cannot be held to be absence without leave.
